headline: Oklahoma State Park Parking and Lodging Permits
reservation: Beavers Bend requires a paid parking permit for all vehicles, which can be purchased via a mobile app on-site or online. Lodge and cabin reservations frequently sell out months in advance; verify current booking windows on the Oklahoma State Parks portal.

days.title: Rivers and Pines

stops.name: Mountain Fork River
stops.detail: Observe the trout-rich waters below the dam where the river winds through tall pines.

stops.name: Forest Heritage Center
stops.detail: Learn about the history of the forest and the specific timber ecology of southeastern Oklahoma.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes from Broken Bow; park roads are paved but narrow.
days.note: Water levels in the river fluctuate based on scheduled dam releases; check local notices.

days.title: Broken Bow Lake Vistas

stops.name: Stephens Gap
stops.detail: Access the shoreline for views of the deep water and islands within the reservoir.

stops.name: Skyline Trail
stops.detail: Hike a portion of this challenging trail for elevated views of the Lower Mountain Fork.

days.driving: Local driving between Hochatown and lake access points takes roughly 15 minutes.
days.note: Trails can be rocky and steep; allow more time than mileage suggests for hiking.

days.title: Cedar Creek and Spills

stops.name: Cedar Creek Golf Course Views
stops.detail: Enjoy the manicured landscape bordering the lake’s edge for a different perspective of the water.

stops.name: Spillway Area
stops.detail: Visit the site where the lake transforms back into the river for dramatic rock formations.

days.driving: Driving between the lodge and northern lake areas takes approximately 20 minutes.
days.note: Parking at the spillway is limited during peak summer weekends.

intel.title: Paid Parking Compliance
intel.text: Vehicle parking is managed through the Premium Parking app at all state park trailheads. Ensure you have the app downloaded before entering areas with limited signal.

intel.title: Forest Coverage
intel.text: Cellular reception is spotty within the deeper canyons of the Mountain Fork River. Use the Forest Heritage Center as a reliable point for emergency landline access.

intel.title: Hochatown Services
intel.text: The town of Hochatown serves as the primary hub for fuel and groceries. There are no fueling stations within the state park boundaries.

intel.title: Autumn Foliage
intel.text: Peak colors typically occur in early to mid-November. Summer visits should account for high humidity and heat indexes often exceeding 95 degrees.

intel.title: Dam Release Safety
intel.text: Sirens indicate water release from the Broken Bow Dam. Waders and swimmers must exit the river immediately when these signals are heard.

plan.arrival: Arrive via Texarkana (TXK), rent a vehicle, and drive two hours northwest. Broken Bow is the primary stop for groceries before entering Hochatown lodging.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for the main park loop; high-clearance is only necessary for specific forestry roads outside the state park.
plan.goldenHour: The Mountain Fork River overlooks at sunset provide soft lighting through the loblolly pines, though canopy density varies.
